annotations: Burned into the image in a separate footer; no subtitle file or subtitle stream is required.
editing: Chapter trims remove unrecorded setup and transitions. Actions play at 1x; purposeful result-reading holds remain. No blanket speed-up.

chapters.title: LeadFlow — the complete lead workflow
chapters.caption: A real Next.js client, Express API and isolated MongoDB. Every interaction in this walkthrough is verified.

chapters.title: Prioritize today; keep the rest in order
chapters.caption: Today is pinned once. Older open follow-ups are red; future follow-ups are neutral. Won/Lost cards are dimmed.

chapters.title: All six status filters
chapters.caption: New, Contacted, Qualified, Proposal Sent, Won and Lost filter both sections. The selected status is stored in the URL.

chapters.title: Search case-insensitively
chapters.caption: Typing sArAh finds Sarah Connor. Search is debounced and shares URL state with the active filter.

chapters.title: Combine filters and search
chapters.caption: The same query under Qualified has no match; switching to Proposal Sent brings Sarah back without navigation.

chapters.title: Literal search and a clear empty state
chapters.caption: Regex punctuation is treated as text. A query containing ( returns no matches safely; clearing it restores the list.

chapters.title: Open the full discussion timeline
chapters.caption: Company and phone stay with the lead. History is newest first, with absolute timestamps and italic system entries.

chapters.title: Save a discussion without changing the reminder
chapters.caption: A note-only save updates the newest history entry and card summary immediately. The existing follow-up is preserved.

chapters.title: Schedule a follow-up from a discussion
chapters.caption: Diana starts in All leads. Adding a note with a local date and time updates her reminder and history in one save.

chapters.title: The lead moves into Today immediately
chapters.caption: No reload is needed. TanStack Query updates the detail and all matching list caches after the API responds.

chapters.title: Earlier today is overdue — and still pinned
chapters.caption: A reminder five minutes ago turns red. Calendar-day membership and elapsed-time overdue styling are separate rules.

chapters.title: Close a lead without showing a false alarm
chapters.caption: Lost leads use a neutral absolute-time chip. Diana stays pinned because her reminder is still on today’s calendar day.

chapters.title: Status and history persist after reload
chapters.caption: Reloading reads the saved Lost status from MongoDB. Reopening the lead as Qualified restores its red past-due chip.

chapters.title: Clear the reminder; keep the discussion history
chapters.caption: Clear follow-up sends an explicit null. The lead moves out of Today, while its existing notes remain available.

chapters.title: Won leads are neutral too
chapters.caption: Bill’s old reminder is red while Contacted, neutral while Won, and red again when reopened. The saved date is unchanged.

chapters.title: Create a lead — required fields are guarded
chapters.caption: This is an intentional validation case: a blank name is rejected in the form before any creation request is sent.

chapters.title: Add a complete contact
chapters.caption: Maya Patel is created as New with optional company and phone. The new card appears immediately with a system-created history entry.

chapters.title: Date and time are required together
chapters.caption: Enabling a follow-up without choosing its date and time shows labelled field errors. The note remains available to correct.

chapters.title: Correct the form and save a future reminder
chapters.caption: Choosing tomorrow completes the same note. Future reminders use the neutral absolute-time chip and stay in All leads.

chapters.title: Optional contact details stay optional
chapters.caption: A second case uses only a name. Noah Kim is still created as New; blank company and phone are normalized to null.

chapters.title: Shareable URL state and a persistent dialog
chapters.caption: Filter, search and open lead ID are represented in the URL. Reloading the page restores the selected timeline.

chapters.title: Keyboard-friendly dialogs
chapters.caption: Escape closes the dialog and returns focus. Tab stays inside the Add Lead dialog, with visible focus treatment.

chapters.title: Loading states on a slower connection
chapters.caption: Only delivery is delayed in this controlled test. The real API response replaces the skeleton once the request completes.

chapters.title: Retry recovers from a network interruption
chapters.caption: An intentional browser-network interruption shows Retry. Clicking it restores the real list; the API stays healthy.

chapters.title: Browser timezone: America/Los_Angeles
chapters.caption: The visible browser uses this timezone. Stored UTC timestamps are unchanged; section membership follows the local calendar day.

chapters.title: Browser timezone: Pacific/Auckland
chapters.caption: The visible browser uses this timezone. Stored UTC timestamps are unchanged; section membership follows the local calendar day.

chapters.title: The API contract is verified too
chapters.caption: These are captured responses, not mock data. Invalid input gets a structured envelope; valid requests keep their documented shapes.

chapters.title: A responsive single-screen workflow
chapters.caption: At 360×640, search remains full width and filters scroll horizontally. The same live data and timeline work on a phone.

chapters.title: Long names and notes do not hide the form
chapters.caption: A real 120-character name/company and 5,000-character note exercise the limit. The title clamps, while the full text stays in the DOM.

chapters.title: The footer stays reachable on small screens
chapters.caption: Date, time and Save Note each fit inside the dialog after scrolling. The same bounds checks also pass at 320×568.

chapters.title: A clean empty instance is ready to use
chapters.caption: This final scene uses the disposable demo database only. An empty list clearly invites the first lead, with the Add action still available.

chapters.title: Verified architecture and delivery
chapters.caption: Typed client → Express validation/services → MongoDB. Local timestamps, cache updates, persistence, accessibility and responsive bounds are checked.

intentional_scenarios: Intentional UI validation, delayed delivery and a controlled browser-network interruption are explicitly labelled. API result cards are populated from actual captured responses. Empty-state chapter clears only the isolated temporary database.
